report:
Summary: There is a clear, interpretable difference. It is a strong bias concentrated on the earliest context positions (primarily position 0, also position 1) in late layers, and the difference vector at those cells points toward vocabulary typical of news/headline or event-descriptive wording (sensational/adjectival tokens and some named-entity/headline fragments). I therefore characterize the difference as: Model B (vs A) injects a stronger “headline / event-descriptive” prior at the start of text.

Why I conclude that
- Where the difference lives: the L2-norm is overwhelmingly concentrated at pos0 (and to a lesser extent pos1) in deep layers, peaking at layer 25 pos0 (322.0) and large through layers ~20–25. That pattern means the two checkpoints mainly differ in how the model represents the initial token(s) late in the forward pass — exactly where a topical or style prior would influence the continuation.
- What direction the difference points to: the logit-lens top tokens for those high-norm cells are dominated by words like tragic / tragedy / iconic / vivid / colorful / timeless / victims / refugees / coming / nearing / blitz / refused / worst / major and similar event-descriptive / headline-like tokens (and some early-layer tokens like “Sale”, “rock”, “cocktail” that suggest topic priors). Position-1 top tokens include numbers/newlines and headline-entity-like tokens (Driver, Names, headlines, van/von). Across many layers the same semantic cluster appears.
- Interpretation: a residual difference that consistently points toward those tokens implies one model’s residuals at the very start bias the network toward producing headliney, sensational, or event-focused continuations relative to the other. Because the effect is concentrated at initial positions and persists in late layers, it behaves like a prior/style/topic signal applied at the start of generation.

Caveats
- Patchscope continuations were not provided here, so I cannot directly show that the difference changes actual sampled continuations (the logit-lens evidence is indirect but consistent).
- The token cluster is somewhat mixed (early-layer tokens include commercial/retail words like “Sale”), so the difference looks like a general topical/style prior rather than a narrow single-label objective. I would not confidently name a single training objective (e.g., “news‑fine‑tuning”) without further causal tests (ablation, patching into generation, or inspecting continuations).

If you want, next steps I would run: (1) inject the top difference cells into prompts and inspect continuations (patchscope samples), (2) ablate the pos0/pos1 late-layer components to confirm causal effect on headlineiness, and (3) check distributions of generated headlines/topics on held-out prompts to quantify the behavioral shift.
